plan.title: Capstone solution emits invalid WI-1000 after valid WI-999

narratives.Description: Both worked addWorkItem listings allocate the next identifier as max-suffix plus one and pad to three digits, so a valid collection whose highest identifier is WI-999 yields WI-1000, which the same module's /^WI-\d{3}$/ validator rejects. The CI rehearsal copy in scripts/capstone-lab.test.mjs derives from the same source and inherits the defect, and no supplied test reaches that boundary. The accepted remedy keeps the bounded WI-NNN namespace and adds a documented RangeError once the highest suffix is 999, pinned across the lab, both listings, the supplied test, and the capstone verifier.
narratives.Overview:
## Learner context

I found this while completing the end-to-end capstone as a 5–10 year engineer, using the learner-facing material only.

- Course baseline: `@deftai/directive@0.119.5`
- Host: macOS/zsh
- Node.js: `v24.20.0`
- Affected material:
  - `labs/capstone-end-to-end.md`, Task 2: allocate the next `WI-NNN` from the highest numeric suffix
  - `solutions/capstone-end-to-end.md`, both worked implementations of `addWorkItem`

## What happened

The supplied validator accepts only `/^WI-\d{3}$/`, but the worked solution calculates the next ID with:

```js
"WI-" + String(highest + 1).padStart(3, "0")
```

For a valid collection whose highest ID is `WI-999`, that expression produces `WI-1000`. A direct evaluation produced:

```json
{"id":"WI-1000","passesValidator":false}
```

The helper's 50-item probe does not reach this boundary. The solution can therefore return an item that its own `validateItems` rejects on the next add, complete, or summary call.

## Expected

The course should define the finite `WI-NNN` namespace boundary, and the worked implementation should either:

1. reject exhaustion before returning an invalid item; or
2. deliberately widen the ID contract and validator.

## Learner pain

The capstone asks for a complete implementation and presents the solution as the comparison, but it leaves the only domain-boundary case undefined and the worked code violates its own invariant. I had to invent behavior not stated by the exercise. My first attempt chose to throw a `RangeError` when the next number would exceed `999`, which passed every guarded stage, but the course gives a learner no basis for knowing whether that is the intended product behavior.

This is especially distracting in a capstone whose core lesson is that tests, acceptance, and independent evidence answer different questions: the protected checks all pass while the worked implementation is internally inconsistent at a reachable valid input.

## Proposed fix

Prefer the bounded-namespace interpretation:

- State explicitly that `WI-NNN` supports `WI-000`/`WI-001` through `WI-999` (whichever lower bound is intended).
- Before constructing the new item, throw a documented `RangeError` when the highest suffix is `999`.
- Add a supplied test or helper-owned independent probe for a collection containing `WI-999`.
- Update both green and reviewed solution listings and explain why the boundary preserves the validator invariant.

An alternative is to change the contract, regex, examples, and prose consistently to an unbounded `WI-<digits>` form, but that is a larger teaching change.

## Suggested acceptance criteria

- The learner-facing contract names exhaustion behavior.
- `addWorkItem` never returns an ID that `validateItems` rejects.
- A protected comparison covers the highest valid suffix.
- The lab, assessment, and explained solution agree on the identifier boundary.
narratives.UserStory: As a learner completing the capstone, I want the worked implementation to refuse identifier exhaustion instead of returning an id its own validator rejects, so that the comparison solution is internally consistent and I do not have to invent product behavior the exercise never states.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. Keep bounded WI-NNN and refuse the unbounded WI-<digits> alternative.
2. Keep max-suffix + 1 allocation, WI-001 from empty, WI-000 as a legal existing identifier, and refuse once a collection already holds WI-999 even when lower identifiers are free.
3. Throw RangeError with one stable phrase after validateItems and the highest-suffix calculation and before constructing the item; pin that type and message on the lab, both solution listings, Valid alternatives, the supplied test, and scripts/verify-capstone.mjs.
4. Put the guard in scripts/capstone-lab.test.mjs greenImplementation after the reduce so reviewedImplementation inherits it; there is no second authored source.
5. Add the frozen supplied WI-999 case to labs/fixtures/capstone-end-to-end/test/work-items.test.mjs, keep the 50-item ordinary-range test, and keep duplicateProbe intact.
6. Land the learner-facing bullet on the lab Task 2 (CAP.2) green list in the same change as that test.
7. Extend scripts/verify-capstone.mjs and add mutation tests; update the authored five supplied tests count.

Round 1 fresh critic, seat family claude. Open critique. Process-only. Reads pinned to `0cb9925d561733ea0907a8f1b450a61416ba1fd6`; in-envelope input is the issue body plus comments through `5760695622`.

## Re-verification

The triage anchors are measured here, not taken from line cites.

- P1 reproduced end-to-end. I extracted the green listing from the `### 3.` slice of `solutions/capstone-end-to-end.md` and ran it behind the fixture CLI: `add "Next" '[{"id":"WI-999","title":"Last","status":"open"}]'` exits `0` and emits `WI-1000`; feeding that exact output back to `summary` exits `1` with `work-item id must use WI-NNN`. The round trip through the two documented verbs breaks.
- The allocation policy is **already** pinned. I implemented the competing reading (next-free-slot with a 999 guard) and ran it against the frozen supplied test: it fails test 1, because `existing=[WI-002]` expects `WI-003` and next-free yields `WI-001`. So the undetermined surface is narrower than the body implies — exactly one branch, `highest === 999`, plus the thrown type and message.
- Lower bound measured: `/^WI-\d{3}$/` accepts `WI-000`, and the allocator seeds `highest` at `0`, so it can never emit it. Reachable allocation range is `WI-001` through `WI-999`.

P1 and P2 both hold. The target survives. The **proposed fix** does not bind as written, for F1 and F2.

## Inventory

Every carrier this change needs already exists; none of the findings below asks for a new mechanism. The contract surfaces are the supplied test `labs/fixtures/capstone-end-to-end/test/work-items.test.mjs`, the Task 2 bullet list at `labs/capstone-end-to-end.md:225`, and the two listings in `solutions/`. The gates are `scripts/verify-capstone.mjs` (cross-surface content assertions) and the staged probes in `labs/fixtures/capstone-end-to-end/capstone-lab.mjs`. Scope control is the two minted records under `.deft/approved-scope/`.

## F1 — blocks-the-design: three allocator copies, and the missed one is what CI executes

Evidence. `git grep 'padStart(3'` at the dispatch SHA returns four sites: `solutions/capstone-end-to-end.md:203`, `solutions/capstone-end-to-end.md:322`, `scripts/capstone-lab.test.mjs:88`, and the expectation formula at `labs/fixtures/capstone-end-to-end/test/work-items.test.mjs:51`. The body names the first two. `scripts/capstone-lab.test.mjs:88` is an inlined reference green implementation carrying the identical expression, and `.github/workflows/capstone-platform-validation.yml:62` runs `node --test scripts/capstone-lab.test.mjs` on `macos-15`, `ubuntu-24.04`, and `windows-2022`.

Failure mode. A change that satisfies "Update both green and reviewed solution listings" leaves the CI reference still emitting `WI-1000`. Either the acceptance criterion "`addWorkItem` never returns an ID that `validateItems` rejects" is false for the one copy the project actually executes, or — if the change also adds a supplied test for the boundary — that untouched reference fails and the platform matrix goes red on all three runners.

Scope consequence, measured. The two halves sit in different minted plans. `scripts/capstone-lab.test.mjs` and the fixture test are in the `fileScope` of `.deft/approved-scope/training.capstone.fixture-runtime.json`; `labs/capstone-end-to-end.md`, `solutions/capstone-end-to-end.md`, `assessments/capstone-end-to-end.md`, and `scripts/verify-capstone.mjs` are in `training.capstone.learning-experience.json`. Both records' `xbriefRelPath` points at an `xbrief/active/...` path that does not exist at this SHA — both briefs are under `xbrief/completed/`.

Disposition consequence. The scope statement is wrong and needs restating over four sites, and the delivery shape is either two PRs along the existing plan boundary or one PR behind a fresh operator mint. Neither existing record is reusable by path.

## F2 — blocks-the-design: "a protected comparison covers the highest valid suffix" is two different changes

Evidence. The criterion is satisfiable as a supplied test or as a helper-owned probe, and the body offers both ("a supplied test or helper-owned independent probe"). The two branches diverge hard against machinery that already exists. `recordGreen` runs the supplied test under `requireSuccess`, so anything added there is a blocking stage gate. `recordPrePrReview` hardcodes exactly one finding, `CAP-P1-001`, and asserts `duplicate.exitCode === 0` with `"Stop: simulated P1 is already resolved; review must classify before editing."` — the pre-PR stage is built around exactly one seeded defect. `scripts/verify-capstone.mjs:572` asserts the green slice does **not** contain the duplicate-title fix. `labs/capstone-end-to-end.md:225` states the green contract as five bullets and names no exhaustion behavior.

Failure mode, supplied-test branch. The guard has to move into the green listing to keep `green` reachable. Task 2's bullet list is the learner's only statement of that contract, and the body's acceptance criteria never name it. A learner who implements those five bullets faithfully now hard-stops at `green` on a rule the lab never gave them. That is the reported pain relocated from a latent inconsistency to a blocking stage.

Failure mode, helper-probe branch. The behavior is enforced and still never stated. `maintainers/CURRICULUM-MAINTENANCE.md` sets learner-ready as completable "from a clean stated start" with "no hidden instructor action" — a protected probe for unstated behavior sits against that bar.

Disposition consequence. The criterion must name one carrier, and the change must land the Task 2 bullet in the same commit. Left as written, the criterion is satisfiable in a shape that makes the lab worse than it is today.

## F3 — sharpens-framing: "exhaustion" misnames the condition

Evidence. Allocation is `Math.max` over existing suffixes plus one, and the supplied test pins that (see Re-verification). A collection holding only `WI-999` has 998 free identifiers and still refuses.

Failure mode. A contract sentence reading "the `WI-NNN` namespace is exhausted" invites reuse-a-free-slot at the boundary, which the frozen supplied test then refuses for an unrelated reason and with an unrelated message — a second round of inventing behavior.

Disposition consequence. State it as monotonic refusal: allocation only ever increases, and `add` refuses once `WI-999` exists even when lower identifiers are free. Pin the thrown type and message too. The course pins its other error contracts by regex (`/nonempty/`, `/not found/`, `/WI-NNN/`), and `scripts/verify-capstone.mjs:657` pins one supplied-test assertion string exactly, so an unpinned message is drift waiting to happen.

## F4 — sharpens-framing: the unbounded alternative is not merely larger, it is defective

Evidence, measured. Under a widened `WI-<digits>` regex, `Number("99999999999999999999") + 1` is `1e20`, equal to the input, so `String(highest + 1)` reproduces the id it was given and `addWorkItem` returns a duplicate identifier for an argv-supplied collection. Separately `Number("0001") === Number("001")`, so the widened regex admits `WI-0001` and `WI-001` as distinct ids sharing one numeric suffix, and `padStart(3, "0")` no longer normalizes either.

Failure mode. `completeWorkItem` matches by exact id string over `items.some(...)`, so a duplicate id makes completion silently pick the first match. That is a worse teaching artifact than the bounded defect being fixed, and it is reachable from the same CLI argument that reaches the current one.

Disposition consequence. Record the alternative as refused on this evidence rather than deferred as "a larger teaching change." Deferred-as-larger leaves it available as the cheap escape for a later arc.

## F5 — sharpens-framing: cross-surface agreement is vacuous on two surfaces and ungated

Evidence. `curriculum/capstone-end-to-end.md` contains zero `WI-` occurrences. `assessments/capstone-end-to-end.md` contains one, `WI-001` in the green evidence row at line 151. `scripts/verify-capstone.mjs` asserts many cross-surface strings and none that binds the identifier contract.

Failure mode. "The lab, assessment, and explained solution agree on the identifier boundary" is satisfiable by editing the lab and the solutions and touching nothing else, and no check detects later drift between the stated bound and the listings.

Disposition consequence. Either narrow the criterion to the surfaces that actually carry the contract — Task 2 and both solution listings — or add the `verify-capstone.mjs` assertion that makes agreement checkable. Prefer the second: that gate is where every other cross-surface agreement in this course is enforced.

## F6 — footnote: lower bound

The validator accepts `WI-000` and the allocator can never emit it, so the stated bound should carry both facts rather than picking one. No failure mode found; this only closes the body's open parenthetical.

## Injection / swarm lens

Triggered, narrowly, and not `N/A` theater: the change edits an input-validation contract over argv-supplied JSON, since `parseItems` in `src/cli.mjs` hands unvalidated parsed JSON straight to `validateItems` and then to `Number(item.id.slice(3))`. The concrete product of that lens is F4 — the widened-regex branch is the one that lets argv reach a duplicate-id state. Nothing else in the target touches authority, identity, concurrency, worktrees, or shared state; the blast radius is course content and a disposable fixture.

## Road not taken

I treated next-free-slot allocation as a second under-determined branch and was going to report it as such. Running it against the frozen supplied test refuted that: the policy is already pinned and only the boundary branch is open. F3 is what survived, and it is a naming finding rather than a second open decision.

## Steelman of the strongest rejected position

The strongest case against acting is close as won't-fix. No guarded stage of the lab constructs a `WI-999` collection, so the defect is unreachable on the documented path; Task 2 already carries five contract bullets on a 474-line lab; and the capstone's lesson is about evidence layers, not domain modelling.

What flips it, and did. The boundary is one documented CLI call away — I reproduced it above through `src/cli.mjs` with no fixture edits — and `maintainers/CURRICULUM-MAINTENANCE.md` sets the learner-ready bar at completable from a clean stated start. I would still flip back if a maintainer policy recorded fictional-app domain completeness as deliberately out of capstone scope. I looked for one in `maintainers/CURRICULUM-MAINTENANCE.md` and `curriculum/capstone-end-to-end.md` and found none; the curriculum page does not mention the identifier format at all.
